claim: NARA is the executive agent for the government-wide CUI program and publishes CUI marking guidance and resources.
allowedLanguage: NARA maintains the government-wide CUI program and publishes marking and handling resources.
prohibitedInference: Do not imply a generic AI classifier can make every CUI determination without agency context or human review.
scopeCaveat: NARA provides CUI program guidance; category-specific handling rules may depend on law, regulation and agency policy.

claim: GSA's public API directory includes http://SAM.gov opportunity, contract-award, federal-hierarchy and related procurement APIs.
allowedLanguage: GSA publishes APIs for several procurement and federal-organization datasets, including http://SAM.gov opportunities and contract awards.
prohibitedInference: Do not imply every API is anonymous, unrestricted, or available to non-federal users at identical limits.
scopeCaveat: Availability, authentication requirements and rate limits differ by API.

claim: Auditors issued 2,485 notices of findings and recommendations to DoD/DoW management in 2025.
allowedLanguage: DoD OIG says auditors issued 2,485 NFRs to management in 2025.
prohibitedInference: Do not imply every NFR is a distinct automatable workflow or public finding.
scopeCaveat: NFRs arose from financial-statement audits; the underlying NFRs are generally not publicly posted.

claim: 15 federal agencies estimated about $186B in improper payments across 64 programs in FY2025.
allowedLanguage: GAO reported approximately $186B in estimated improper payments across 64 programs at 15 agencies in FY2025.
prohibitedInference: Do not say AI could save $186B or that all improper payments are fraud.
scopeCaveat: Estimate reported by 15 agencies across 64 programs for FY2025; improper payments include overpayments, underpayments, fraud and other causes.

claim: NIST's AI RMF and Generative AI Profile are intended to help organizations manage AI risks across the AI lifecycle.
allowedLanguage: NIST's AI RMF provides a voluntary framework for managing AI risks, with a companion Generative AI Profile.
prohibitedInference: Do not present the AI RMF as a mandatory federal certification unless a separate requirement makes it so.
scopeCaveat: AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary and is under revision; the Generative AI Profile is a companion resource.

claim: About $153B of FY2025 estimated improper payments were overpayments.
allowedLanguage: GAO reported roughly $153B in overpayments within the FY2025 improper-payment estimate.
prohibitedInference: Do not equate overpayments with recoverable savings or fraud.
scopeCaveat: Part of the same FY2025 government-wide improper-payment estimate; roughly 82% of the total.

claim: Treasury Fiscal Data provides machine-readable federal financial datasets with APIs, historical/current data and data dictionaries.
allowedLanguage: Treasury Fiscal Data publishes federal financial datasets in machine-readable formats with APIs and metadata.
prohibitedInference: Do not imply every Treasury dataset is real-time.
scopeCaveat: Describes the Fiscal Data platform generally; update cadence varies by dataset.

claim: NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3 applies security requirements to components of nonfederal systems that process, store or transmit CUI.
allowedLanguage: SP 800-171 Rev. 3 defines recommended security requirements for nonfederal system components that process, store or transmit CUI.
prohibitedInference: Do not characterize the publication itself as an automatic certification or authorization.
scopeCaveat: NIST publication scope is protection of CUI in nonfederal systems and organizations under the conditions described by the publication.

claim: USAspending's public API exposes comprehensive federal award and account-level spending data and its listed endpoints do not currently require authorization.
allowedLanguage: USAspending exposes machine-readable federal spending data through a public API; the endpoint documentation currently says authorization is not required.
prohibitedInference: Do not imply all federal financial data is public or that no rate/usage constraints exist.
scopeCaveat: Applies to the public USAspending API and current documented endpoints; endpoint behavior can change.

claim: DoD/DoW tracks funds through more than 426 financial systems.
allowedLanguage: DoD OIG describes a financial environment spanning more than 426 financial systems.
prohibitedInference: Do not imply all 426 systems are obsolete, noncompliant, or candidates for replacement.
scopeCaveat: Figure is stated in the OIG's explanation of FY2025 financial-statement complexity.

claim: The FY2025 DoD/DoW financial statement audit identified 26 material weaknesses.
allowedLanguage: The FY2025 audit identified 26 material weaknesses.
prohibitedInference: Do not claim 26 problems could be fixed by AI or software alone.
scopeCaveat: FY2025 agency-wide financial-statement audit; material weaknesses are significant control deficiencies and are not all software defects.

claim: OpenRouter's 2025 State of AI study analyzed more than 100 trillion tokens of real-world LLM interactions and observed growing programming usage and agentic inference.
allowedLanguage: OpenRouter's 2025 study analyzed more than 100T tokens on its platform and reported growing programming usage and agentic inference.
prohibitedInference: Do not generalize OpenRouter's traffic distribution to all AI usage without qualification.
scopeCaveat: The study covers traffic observed on OpenRouter, not the entire AI market or all enterprise AI usage.
